findings.text: ioremap_page_range and vmap_page_range accept virtual bounds plus physical address plus protection and report zero for success while performing no work in this configuration. They serve as portable fallbacks where no real implementation is present.
devm_ioport_map reports unavailability with a null result and devm_ioport_unmap accepts device plus address and does nothing. Callers must treat null as unavailable port access.

pci_remap_cfgspace first attempts a non posted mapping of offset and length and on failure falls back to a posted mapping. A macro alias exposes the same name, indicating an overridable generic implementation.

Generic write combining and memory type helpers are no operation defaults: adding write combining reports zero, deleting or freeing does nothing, index lookup reports minus one, reserving write combining memory type reports zero, and device port availability reports one. Macro aliases mark them as defined so architectures may override.

MEMREMAP_WB occupies bit zero and MEMREMAP_WT occupies bit one and MEMREMAP_WC occupies bit two and MEMREMAP_ENC occupies bit three and MEMREMAP_DEC occupies bit four. Each value is a single bit suitable for combination.

range_is_allowed has two variants governing physical range permission. One variant computes byte bounds from page frame plus length and checks every constituent page for device memory permission, denying with zero on any failure and allowing with one otherwise. The other variant unconditionally allows with one.
iowrite64be is marked as non atomic and directed to low then high half implementations under two alternative macro spellings. The marker lets callers know the store may tear into two 32 bit accesses.

When support is enabled, file and task cancellation delegate to a shared cancel routine only if the current task holds ring state, with a flag distinguishing file exit from task exit. Release delegates only if ring or restriction state exists, and fork delegates only if restriction state exists, otherwise reporting zero without work.

When support is disabled, cancellation and release do nothing, fork reports zero, opcode naming returns an empty string, and file type testing always reports false. These provide link time no operation replacements.

IORING_URING_CMD_CANCELABLE occupies bit thirty and IORING_URING_CMD_REISSUE occupies bit thirty one in a 32 bit field, and IO_URING_CMD_TASK_WORK_ISSUE_FLAGS equals the deferred completion flag. The high placement keeps them separate from lower command specific bits.

The pass through command record carries a file reference, a submission entry reference, a numeric sub operation, flags, a 32 byte inline private area available for free use, and 8 bytes of unused space. Related accessors expose the submission command bytes and the inline area with compile time size validation.

Access to embedded command bytes and private data is guarded by compile time size limits: single entry access must fit within one submission entry command area, double entry access within two entries, private type must fit within the 32 byte inline area, and generic request to command conversion validates the target size.

Fixed buffer import, vector import, buffer selection, buffer registration for requests and vectors, buffer unregistration and network socket dispatch all report EOPNOTSUPP in this configuration, with buffer selection carrying the error in a result wrapper. They define the interface shape without providing behavior.

Completion helpers forward a status plus optional second result plus issue flags to a shared internal completion with a width selector for standard versus extended results. Context access derives ring context and owning task from the enclosing request, and task work conversion recovers the command from a deferred work descriptor.

Deferred execution helpers queue a callback for execution in task context, with a lazy wake variant that requests delayed wakeup and an immediate completion variant. Marking cancelable and issuing blocking are no operation and multishot posting reports true in this configuration.

IOU_F_TWQ_LAZY_WAKE uses value one and IOU_F_TWQ_IN_WAKE uses value two. IO_URING_F_COMPLETE_DEFER uses one, IO_URING_F_UNLOCKED uses two, IO_URING_F_MULTISHOT uses four, IO_URING_F_IOWQ uses eight, IO_URING_F_INLINE uses sixteen, IO_URING_F_NONBLOCK uses the integer minimum, IO_URING_F_SQE128 uses bit eight, IO_URING_F_CQE32 uses bit nine, IO_URING_F_IOPOLL uses bit ten, IO_URING_F_CANCEL uses bit eleven, IO_URING_F_COMPAT uses bit twelve. Buffer direction bits mirror iterator direction positions for destination and source.

IO_RINGFD_REG_MAX is sixteen. IO_RING_F_DRAIN_NEXT uses bit zero, IO_RING_F_OP_RESTRICTED uses bit one, IO_RING_F_REG_RESTRICTED uses bit two, IO_RING_F_OFF_TIMEOUT_USED uses bit three, IO_RING_F_DRAIN_ACTIVE uses bit four, IO_RING_F_HAS_EVFD uses bit five, IO_RING_F_TASK_COMPLETE uses bit six, IO_RING_F_LOCKLESS_CQ uses bit seven, IO_RING_F_SYSCALL_IOPOLL uses bit eight, IO_RING_F_POLL_ACTIVATED uses bit nine, IO_RING_F_DRAIN_DISABLED uses bit ten, IO_RING_F_COMPAT uses bit eleven, IO_RING_F_IOWQ_LIMITS_SET uses bit twelve, IO_RING_F_RESTRICT_INHERITED uses bit thirteen.

Shared rings pair head and tail counters for submission and completion with masks and power of two capacities, dropped submission and lost completion counters, submission flags written by kernel and completion flags written by application, and a trailing cache aligned completion entry array. A tiny head tail pair type underlies both sides.

Submission head and completion tail are owned by the kernel while submission tail and completion head are owned by the application. Masks equal capacity minus one and convert offsets to indices, dropped and overflow counts accumulate without ordering guarantees, and the application must order tail update before checking need wakeup while the kernel refreshes completion entries on each production.

Per task ring state holds cached references, last context, owning task, work queue, consumer cursor for task delivered work, fixed sixteen entry array of registered ring files, index tree, wait queue, cancel and tracked inflight counters, per cpu inflight accounting, fallback work for post exit draining, and a cache aligned task work queue plus callback. Only the task itself or fallback work pops the cursor.

Ring context groups state into cache aligned sections for read mostly setup plus references and clock plus notification, submission indices plus entries plus file and buffer tables plus node and request caches plus poll lists plus cancel hash plus cancelable list plus loop callback, completion entry cache plus tail plus event file plus wait parameters, cross CPU task work plus completion signaling, and timeout lists, followed by overflow, wait identity, credentials, polling thread linkage, allocation bounds, restrictions, accounting trees, reference completion and resizing protection.

Filter updates serialize with a spin lock and defer reclamation by read copy update with copy on write semantics for restriction changes. Submission tables and poll structures serialize with a mutex except single threaded poll mode, completion allocation serializes with a completion spin lock, timeouts with a raw spin lock, task context list with a dedicated mutex nesting under submission lock, and resize versus map races with a map mutex.

Work handling uses intrusive single link nodes plus first last list heads, a multi producer queue with tail and stub, and a work item carrying list linkage plus atomic flags plus cancel sequence. Resources use counted node arrays plus bitmap allocation with hint, cache aligned hash buckets plus table sizing, mapped regions of pages plus address plus counts plus flags, and a vector union of IO or block segments plus capacity.

Submission uses head last link pairs, a state record with free and completion lists plus plug and batch counters, and a bounded object cache with entry array plus counts plus element size plus clear flag. Restrictions combine operation bitmaps plus filter reference plus allowed and required flag bytes plus presence booleans. Buffer selection pairs a list reference with a union of user address or signed error.

Lazy wake must not be used for requests producing more than one completion and is ignored unless deferred task execution is enabled. Signaling completion event file from wait queue wake context must defer to avoid reentering provider locks through event polling. Non atomic 64 bit stores may be observed torn, and page by page permission checks assume stable device memory policy during the walk.
Each header defines a unique inclusion guard macro so repeated inclusion yields a single definition set. The guards carry no behavioral effect beyond preventing double processing.
